Added a covering test.\\n- The fix is folded into the branch\\u0027s existing commit \\u00601edd6400\\u0060 (was \\u0060e717e809\\u0060), not a new commit \\u2014 tree identity vs. the pre-fold tip is verified empty.\\n- Gotcha for future rebase/fixup work on this branch: \\u0060git fetch origin main\\u0060 here pulls in real, unrelated commits from other concurrently-landing tasks \\u2014 don\\u0027t blindly \\u0060rebase --autosquash origin/main\\u0060 after fetching; compute \\u0060git merge-base \\u003Cbranch-tip\\u003E origin/main\\u0060 first and rebase against that if you want to fold a fixup without dragging in main\\u0027s advancement. Named behaviours: jump in and out of interactive sessions freely on demand; claim a task queued behind other work as an out-of-band implementation path; when dependency edges exist, warn rather than refuse - name the tasks meant to land first, ask if sure, and let it be the human\\u0027s call; human-friendly throughout, human able to override everything. Trigger and strongest argument: Brian could not work out how to start an interactive session on 5de98032 the day he wanted to - if it confuses the builder it will be ridiculously confusing to a normal user; same first-run-experience class as f4cce412. Discovery raw material (verified in code by the Windows Feedback triage session): (1) h9k task work launches Claude as a foreground child in the caller\\u0027s terminal, and claim \\u002B worktree cut \\u002B prompt assembly \\u002B launch are one indivisible command - no h9k task claim stops short of launching, so an orchestrator cannot trigger or even prepare a session; (2) nothing surfaces the coordinates - worktree path and branch print once at launch, task show carries neither, and the recorded Claude session id (InteractiveSessionStarted/Ended) is surfaced nowhere; (3) re-entry deliberately mints a fresh session id rather than resuming the recorded one (decision #103\\u0027s choice, confirmed in LaunchInteractiveClaudeAsync: new guid, never --resume) - worktree and branch carry over, the conversation does not, and Brian wants the opposite, trade-off real in both directions; (4) ClaimInteractively and TaskWorkCommand refuse anything not Queued, Blocked included - the warn-rather-than-refuse ask lands exactly there. Slice sketch for discovery, not a proposal: 688a1ccf (published, queued) is arguably this epic\\u0027s first slice rather than a standalone fix - decide membership at discovery; surface the coordinates on task show; claim across a dependency edge with warning and confirmation; detached launch under a name, so a session starts without occupying the caller\\u0027s terminal and an orchestrator can trigger it - the piece with real cross-platform cost and probably the epic\\u0027s centre of gravity; re-entry resumes the recorded session. Design fact that changes the shape: cross-session messaging already exists outside hall9k (two Claude sessions on one machine can list and message each other), so \\u0022the orchestrator talks to the task\\u0027s session\\u0022 needs no hall9k messaging layer at all provided the session is running and named - detached-launch-under-a-name is the load-bearing piece. APPENDED OBSERVATION (2026-09-01 evening, Brian\\u0027s direction): the session mesh already includes the headless agents. Observed twice without looking for it: the daemon\\u0027s dispatched review-lens sessions appeared in the orchestrator window\\u0027s peer-session list, addressable under their worktree-derived names (wt-e5c0d371-52dd4812-9f and -b6), and Brian\\u0027s interactive claim session on 5de98032 held a full two-way relay with the orchestrator window. So detached-launch-under-a-name is even cheaper than the original note assumed - headless runs are ALREADY launched detached and ALREADY named, just accidentally (by worktree) rather than deliberately. What discovery should add on top: a naming convention worth addressing (task id and role, not worktree suffix), and messaging RULES as first-class design - operator-to-build-session is legitimate steering, anyone-to-review-lens is contamination of the fresh-context independence guarantee and should be treated as forbidden, and messaging a COMPLETED session is hazardous because a send resumes it from its transcript, so a dead run session could wake and act in a worktree the daemon considers settled. Also record the audit tension: a cross-session message steers a run through a channel the event store never sees, which cuts against the platform\\u0027s intent-and-outcome-on-streams posture; the platform-native mid-run dialogue remains decision #5\\u0027s ask-and-exit design, and the mesh is the observation-and-emergency channel, not the routine one - unless discovery deliberately decides Trigger and strongest argument: Brian could not work out how to start an interactive session on 5de98032 the day he wanted to - if it confuses the builder it will be ridiculously confusing to a normal user; same first-run-experience class as f4cce412. Discovery raw material (verified in code by the Windows Feedback triage session): (1) h9k task work launches Claude as a foreground child in the caller\\u0027s terminal, and claim \\u002B worktree cut \\u002B prompt assembly \\u002B launch are one indivisible command - no h9k task claim stops short of launching, so an orchestrator cannot trigger or even prepare a session; (2) nothing surfaces the coordinates - worktree path and branch print once at launch, task show carries neither, and the recorded Claude session id (InteractiveSessionStarted/Ended) is surfaced nowhere; (3) re-entry deliberately mints a fresh session id rather than resuming the recorded one (decision #103\\u0027s choice, confirmed in LaunchInteractiveClaudeAsync: new guid, never --resume) - worktree and branch carry over, the conversation does not, and Brian wants the opposite, trade-off real in both directions; (4) ClaimInteractively and TaskWorkCommand refuse anything not Queued, Blocked included - the warn-rather-than-refuse ask lands exactly there. Slice sketch for discovery, not a proposal: 688a1ccf (published, queued) is arguably this epic\\u0027s first slice rather than a standalone fix - decide membership at discovery; surface the coordinates on task show; claim across a dependency edge with warning and confirmation; detached launch under a name, so a session starts without occupying the caller\\u0027s terminal and an orchestrator can trigger it - the piece with real cross-platform cost and probably the epic\\u0027s centre of gravity; re-entry resumes the recorded session. Design fact that changes the shape: cross-session messaging already exists outside hall9k (two Claude sessions on one machine can list and message each other), so \\u0022the orchestrator talks to the task\\u0027s session\\u0022 needs no hall9k messaging layer at all provided the session is running and named - detached-launch-under-a-name is the load-bearing piece. APPENDED OBSERVATION (2026-09-01 evening, Brian\\u0027s direction): the session mesh already includes the headless agents. Observed twice without looking for it: the daemon\\u0027s dispatched review-lens sessions appeared in the orchestrator window\\u0027s peer-session list, addressable under their worktree-derived names (wt-e5c0d371-52dd4812-9f and -b6), and Brian\\u0027s interactive claim session on 5de98032 held a full two-way relay with the orchestrator window. So detached-launch-under-a-name is even cheaper than the original note assumed - headless runs are ALREADY launched detached and ALREADY named, just accidentally (by worktree) rather than deliberately. What discovery should add on top: a naming convention worth addressing (task id and role, not worktree suffix), and messaging RULES as first-class design - operator-to-build-session is legitimate steering, anyone-to-review-lens is contamination of the fresh-context independence guarantee and should be treated as forbidden, and messaging a COMPLETED session is hazardous because a send resumes it from its transcript, so a dead run session could wake and act in a worktree the daemon considers settled. Also record the audit tension: a cross-session message steers a run through a channel the event store never sees, which cuts against the platform\\u0027s intent-and-outcome-on-streams posture; the platform-native mid-run dialogue remains decision #5\\u0027s ask-and-exit design, and the mesh is the observation-and-emergency channel, not the routine one - unless discovery deliberately decides otherwise and records why.\\n DESIGN RULINGS FROM THE 2026-09-01 EVENING EXPLORATION (Brian): (1) Two modes structure the epic - start-it-mine (a deliberate human kick-off: ceiling-exempt like an interactive claim already is under #103, edge-warned with acknowledgment, dispatched headless but named and reachable) and take-it-over (hooking into a run the dispatcher started). (2) Naming: every dispatched agent session gets a human-readable name carrying task id and role (5de98032-build, 5de98032-review-adversarial), because the interaction rules key on role. (3) RULING, reversing the appended observation\\u0027s earlier position: review lenses MAY be interacted with - the human asking \\u0022tell me what you are finding\\u0022 or \\u0022check with me before you finalize\\u0022 changes the reporting protocol, not the judgment inputs, and is the park moved upstream to the human\\u0027s initiative; the default stays untouched passes, the contact-time warning states the observer-effect cost (human presence shifts what a reviewer attends to), and the platform advises, never refuses. (4) The escape-hatch invariant: every outside interaction an agent has is logged to hall9k unconditionally, prompt-mandated, even if the interacting party demands otherwise - best-effort by nature and worth it anyway; a logged override makes the record say \\u0022human directed this\\u0022 instead of lying about provenance. (5) Human overrides delivered mid-pass should land as first-class events the settled-rulings machinery (#88) carries forward, so a mid-pass ruling teaches future passes exactly as a park ruling does. (6) Instruments-first as guidance, not law: prefer the run\\u0027s own records for observation and the CLI/daemon channels where they are efficient, with direct agent-to-agent contact as the human\\u0027s choice whenever they want it - a judgment call, both doors always open. Slice sketch for discovery, not a proposal: 688a1ccf (published, queued) is arguably this epic\\u0027s first slice rather than a standalone fix - decide membership at discovery; surface the coordinates on task show; claim across a dependency edge with warning and confirmation; detached launch under a name, so a session starts without occupying the caller\\u0027s terminal and an orchestrator can trigger it - the piece with real cross-platform cost and probably the epic\\u0027s centre of gravity; re-entry resumes the recorded session. Design fact that changes the shape: cross-session messaging already exists outside hall9k (two Claude sessions on one machine can list and message each other), so \\u0022the orchestrator talks to the task\\u0027s session\\u0022 needs no hall9k messaging layer at all provided the session is running and named - detached-launch-under-a-name is the load-bearing piece.
